clue.text: Part of Ascot clearly seen behind champion

indicators.note: the word for clearly is placed after the word for champion

parts.note: to champion a cause is to back it
clearly, plainly, in a direct way: straight

explanation.surface: A racegoer at Ascot spots the winning horse in plain view.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a famous English racecourse; the home straight there is preceded by the back straight on the far side of the track.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse's back straight is the stretch farthest from the stands, one section of a course like Ascot's.

clue.text: Toff upset about poorly cut short jacket

indicators.note: the reversed word for toff goes around the trimmed word for poorly
in a down clue upset means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a toff or swell is a nob

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is lopped off the word

parts.note: done poorly means done in a lousy way

explanation.surface: An upper-class snob is annoyed by a badly tailored jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NOB into BON; 'cut' trims LOUSY to LOUS, which BON goes 'about' to give B-LOUS-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A blouson is a short loose jacket gathered at the waist, so it is a type of short coat.

clue.text: Recent jog with uncle going around ugly high-rise area

indicators.note: going around suggests the letters spinning into a new order

explanation.surface: A man has just been out running with his uncle around a grim tower-block estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' reads like the route of the run, but it is the anagram signal; 'with' only joins the fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete jungle is an idiom for a bleak urban area dominated by tall concrete buildings.

clue.text: Fresh uprising to the south in Asian country

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: fresh air or a breezy room: airy

explanation.surface: A new revolt breaks out in the southern part of an Asian nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns AIRY to YRIA; the blog reads it as AIRY plus S all turned, which gives the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a country in western Asia, on the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Goes without starter, fish and wine

indicators.note: without starter means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: has a go, attempts: tries
the ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone skips the first course and has fish and a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without starter' drops the T from TRIES to leave RIES; the dining surface makes 'starter' look like a course.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white grape variety and the dry or sweet white wine made from it.

clue.text: Clue given in hide-and-seek

indicators.note: given in says the letters sit inside the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A hint is offered during a children's game of hide-and-seek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given in' points to the letters spanning hIDE-And.
explanation.definitionFit: Clue is used for notion, as in having no clue meaning having no inkling at all.

clue.text: Workers getting glum extremely easily

parts.note: farm or factory workers are hands
feeling glum is feeling down

explanation.surface: The staff become miserable with very little effort.
explanation.definitionFit: To win hands down is an idiom for winning with no effort at all, so very easily.

clue.text: In space he lands up somehow over the moon

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive in some other, unknown order

explanation.surface: An astronaut touches down in space and is delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is only a link; the fodder is SPACE HE LANDS UP, rearranged as 'somehow' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleased as Punch and over the moon are both idioms for extremely delighted.

clue.text: Couple at end of boozy party crossing city for Cajun music

indicators.note: a couple, two letters, taken from the end of the word boozy
the party word lies across the city abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: a do is a party or social function
EC is the postal district for the City of London

explanation.surface: Two people arrive at the tail end of a drunken party in town to hear some Cajun music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple at end of' takes two letters, not one, from the tail of boozy. EC is the postcode for the City of London, its financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Zydeco is a lively dance music of Louisiana's Creole and Cajun communities, built on accordion and washboard.

clue.text: One who has depressing experience missing daughter

indicators.note: missing means the abbreviation for daughter is taken away

parts.note: a downer is something depressing

explanation.surface: Someone who suffers a sad time because their daughter is absent.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is a person who possesses or holds something, so someone who has it.

clue.text: Like Chinaman, but not as friend for ever?

indicators.note: but not says the following word is removed from the word before

parts.note: a man from China is of the East, so oriental or eastern
taken as written
a friend is an ally

explanation.surface: Someone is described as like a Chinese man, though never as a companion, permanently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' strips the word as from the adjective for the man from China. 'Chinaman' is a dated, now offensive term for a Chinese man.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means without end, lasting for all time.

clue.text: Possible to order a lobster to be cooked?

indicators.note: cooked hints at letters that are worked over and rearranged, like cooked books

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether a lobster may be ordered to be prepared in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like ordering a meal, but the definition means able to be put in order; 'to be cooked' signals the anagram of A LOBSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sortable means capable of being sorted, arranged into some sequence.

clue.text: Park it in park perhaps

definitions.meaning: an ... car, a vehicle you might park
a landed property, such as grounds or parkland around a country house

explanation.walkthrough: An ESTATE car is the British term for a station wagon. 'in' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate is both a British car with a rear loading door and a large area of landed property.

clue.text: Bean I received in payment as provider of sustenance?

parts.note: bean is slang for the head, as is nut

indicators.note: the payment word takes in the letter I

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for property

explanation.surface: A bean plant is accepted as payment as a source of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bean' looks like food but is the head; 'received in' places I inside RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrient is a substance that nourishes, so it supplies sustenance.

clue.text: Saucy about very small bust

indicators.note: the word for saucy goes around the letter for very

parts.note: saucy, cheeky: insolent
v is the small-letter abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about a tiny chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts V inside INSOLENT; 'bust' looks like a chest but means broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Bust is slang for bankrupt, having no means to pay debts.

clue.text: Don's approval during brother's dance

indicators.note: during says one word happens inside another

parts.note: bro is short for brother
a Spanish don cheers olé

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman approves of his sibling's dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a Spanish gentleman, whose cheer of approval is the bullring shout; 'during' sets it inside the short word for brother.
explanation.definitionFit: The bolero is a Spanish dance in triple time.

clue.text: Desperate way to talk, overcome by drink

indicators.note: overcome by means held inside the word for drink

parts.note: to lap is to drink like a cat
St is short for street, a way
to gas is to talk idly

explanation.surface: Someone resorts to a desperate manner of speaking, overwhelmed by alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcome by' means the way-and-talk pair sits wholly inside the drink word; 'to' only links. Last-gasp is used as an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-gasp effort is one made at the final moment in desperation.

clue.text: Alter newspaper item in every way

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement in a newspaper
Chambers gives just as quite, absolutely, indeed

explanation.surface: An editor changes a newspaper article completely.
explanation.walkthrough: JUST in its rare sense of absolutely, as in 'just perfect'.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust something is to alter it slightly, adapting or modifying it.

clue.text: Scrape with a nail point

parts.note: a brad is a thin flat nail
E for east, a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone scratches with the tip of a nail.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to scrape or wear away by rubbing.

clue.text: State support

definitions.meaning: to state is to assert or declare
to support is to provide for or keep up

explanation.definitionFit: Maintain means both to assert a claim and to keep something going or provide for someone.

clue.text: Short message in TV fund-raiser raised less cash at the end

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is read upwards, backwards
less means a letter is taken away

parts.note: a telethon is a long television broadcast raising money for charity

indicators.note: at the end picks the final letter of cash

explanation.surface: A brief note about a TV charity show that ended up raising less money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the end' gives H from cash; 'less' removes it from TELETHON, giving TELETON, which 'raised' turns to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded sheet for writing a brief note.

clue.text: Before deer returned, managed to get someone's goat

indicators.note: before puts the word for managed in front

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it: ran

indicators.note: returned means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: an elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: Having run things before the deer came back, someone gets annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns ELK to KLE; 'to' only links. To get someone's goat is to irritate them.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to cause lasting irritation or resentment.

clue.text: Run out of town for a slow cooker?

indicators.note: out of means the run abbreviation is taken from the town

parts.note: Stockport is a town in Greater Manchester
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone flees town for a gentle cooking appliance.
explanation.walkthrough: STOCKPORT is a town near Manchester in northern England; 'out of' takes the R out.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockpot simmers for hours making stock, so it cooks slowly.

clue.text: Stuff filling empty, overturned picnic hamper

indicators.note: one word fills the space inside another
overturned means read upwards, backwards
empty means the word's inside is removed, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: to stuff is to cram or ram

explanation.surface: Food fills a picnic basket that has been emptied and tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps only the outer letters of picnic, 'overturned' flips that pair, and 'filling' sets the stuffing word between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper is to cramp, restrict movement or progress.

clue.text: Having left from port, see capital

indicators.note: L for left is taken away from the port name

parts.note: Kiel is a German Baltic port
V is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: Having departed from harbour, a traveller visits a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is L, and 'Having left from' takes it out of KIEL; V adds 'see'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiev, now usually spelt Kyiv, is the capital of Ukraine.

clue.text: Hedonistic existence of unusually active old characters

indicators.note: unusually means put in an unusual, unexpected order

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeking life led by remarkably energetic elderly people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like people but just means letters; 'of' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolce vita, Italian for sweet life, describes a life of luxurious self-indulgence.

clue.text: Cancel yearly publication lacking second article

indicators.note: lacking means a piece is missing from the word

parts.note: an annual is a book published once a year
A is an indefinite article; here the second A in the word goes

explanation.surface: A yearly magazine is cancelled for lacking a second feature.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void, to cancel officially.

clue.text: At pet shop I've bust headgear

indicators.note: bust means broken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A customer at a pet shop has damaged a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' signals the anagram of AT PET SHOP IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stovepipe hat is a tall cylindrical silk hat, as worn by Abraham Lincoln.
